correctness.rationale: Proof gives exact fiberwise cross semantics, matching/Koenig vertex-cover dichotomy, all minimal counterexamples as three-edge matchings or four edges from two same-shore centers, three neighbor-intersection cases, and disjoint combinatorial type counts. The classical Koenig theorem is correctly applied to all finite simple bipartite graphs, including isolated vertices. The extracted verifier confirms 16 full alphabet rectangles through 4x4, direct split semantics through 3x3, and all 2x2x2 subsets. Computations are not relied on for the general quantifiers.

originality.rationale: The original primary Theorem 22 already establishes 4-coherence for this same disjunction, and a published exact satisfying-team enumerator already uses a row-column cross normal form. Neither inspected primary statement gives the complete six minimal non-coverable graph classes, distinguishes 3-assignment from 4-assignment obstructions across all alphabets, or counts their labelled multiplicities. These are derived here with a matching/cover argument. Distinct published-finding corpus obstruction results use different variable identifications; this prevents specialization. Priority remains qualified by accessible-source limits.

value.rationale: The complete minimal forbidden-subteam basis is a natural and consequential refinement of the already-known 4-coherence cutoff for a canonical two-dependence-atom formula. It exposes the possible 3-row failures, classifies all four-row structural mechanisms including shore orientation, and gives a reusable closed labelled census for every determinant and consequent alphabet size. This enumerates all minimal counterexamples for testing database dependence splits rather than providing arbitrary finite instances or only a routine fixed-size calculation. Scope and historical uncertainty are explicitly bounded.
